title: NetBox Labs Partners with NVIDIA and Grafana Labs, Announces New Infrastructure Intelligence Platform Capabilities
headline: NetBox Labs adds agents and ties in NVIDIA, Grafana
summary: NetBox Labs announced partnerships with NVIDIA and Grafana Labs at NetBox Evolve 2026, introducing NetBox Designs, NetBox Analytics, NetBox Agents, and integrations with NVIDIA Configuration Manager (NVCM), Arista CloudVision, AWS VPC IPAM, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard. The platform now serves as the central intelligence layer for AI datacenter and enterprise infrastructure operations.
why: NetBox becomes native to NVIDIA DSX OS and expands its source-of-truth role for AI infrastructure automation; critical for network teams scaling AI workloads that depend on accurate infrastructure data and integrated observability.
detail: NetBox Labs announced major platform expansions at its inaugural NetBox Evolve conference on October 13, 2026. NVIDIA integration makes NetBox the primary system of record for NVIDIA Configuration Manager within NVIDIA DSX OS, embedding NetBox at the center of GPU cluster fabric automation. New capabilities include NetBox Agents (pre-built agents for change review, compliance checking, data quality, and imports), NetBox Analytics (launching in November) with NetBox Visual Explorer for visualizing large-scale datacenter and network infrastructure, and new integrations with Arista CloudVision, AWS VPC IPAM, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard (available in October), plus preview integrations with Palo Alto Panorama, Tenable, and Kubernetes launching end of October. Grafana Labs partnership integrates NetBox with Grafana's observability stack. The announcement positions NetBox as the data foundation for agentic infrastructure operations—directly addressing the 2026 reality that 0% of enterprises currently operate with agentic NetOps, though Gartner forecasts 50% will by 2030. The platform now supports both human operators and AI agents designing and running complex infrastructure.

title: LogicMonitor Unveils New Operating Model for AI-Driven IT Operations at Elevate 2026
headline: LogicMonitor folds Catchpoint data into governed AI operations model
summary: LogicMonitor announced a new operating model combining Envision platform, Edwin AI, and Catchpoint digital experience data to move IT operations from reactive alerts to governed AI-driven investigation and remediation across infrastructure, incident investigation, and automated action.
why: Organizations using Edwin AI achieved 313% ROI; the platform enables NOC and SRE teams to reduce alert noise by up to 97% through ML-driven correlation and automate triage across fragmented monitoring stacks.
detail: LogicMonitor's Autonomous IT architecture consolidates five areas: enterprise data foundation, unified context, AI-led governed action, embedded experience, and trust/governance controls. Edwin AI applies unsupervised ML to correlate alerts, detect anomalies, identify root causes, and suppress redundant alert floods. The platform integrates with MCP for compatible AI clients, enabling agentic operations while maintaining human oversight. This represents a fundamental shift in NOC practice from reactive alert response to proactive incident investigation with bounded autonomous action—critical for teams managing complex hybrid and multi-cloud estates at scale.

title: OpenTelemetry 2026: CNCF Graduation, Kubernetes Processor, and Continuous Profiling as Fourth Signal
headline: OpenTelemetry graduates and adds continuous profiling as fourth signal
summary: OpenTelemetry achieved CNCF graduation in May 2026; Kubernetes Attributes Processor reached v1.0.0 in September; continuous profiling (eBPF-based) entered alpha with GA target Q3/Q4 2026. GenAI Semantic Conventions became de facto standard for AI observability, enabling hallucination rates and model quality metrics alongside traditional SRE golden signals.
why: OTLP is now cemented as industry standard post-graduation, eliminating vendor lock-in and enabling cross-signal correlation essential for meaningful AIOps without noise. Unified telemetry foundation enables NOC automation to correlate network, application, and infrastructure signals from single instrumentation.
detail: OpenTelemetry graduated CNCF in May 2026, ranking second only to Kubernetes in project velocity with 12,000+ contributors from 2,800+ companies. Traces, metrics, and logs are now stable across every major language SDK; continuous profiling (via Parca, Pyroscope, Grafana Beyla) is increasingly integrated into OTel pipeline, providing code-level visibility alongside business metrics. GenAI semantic conventions moved to dedicated specification mid-2026 and are now universally supported. For network and infrastructure observability, OTel graduation removes vendor lock-in and enables consistent instrumentation across network devices, applications, and infrastructure—allowing NOC teams to correlate events from multiple sources (NetFlow, syslog, traces, metrics) under single trace context for unified root cause analysis.

title: Micas Networks Launches Tomahawk 6 Co-Packaged Optics Switch, Bringing Independent Vendor Option to Broadcom CPO Ecosystem
headline: Micas brings co-packaged optics switches beyond the hyperscalers
summary: On October 13, Micas Networks announced three new switches built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 chip, including a compact co-packaged optics switch using Broadcom Tomahawk 6-Davisson, with production expected in early 2027. This brings CPO technology to independent vendors—previously limited to hyperscalers.
why: Co-packaged optics technology (70% power reduction versus pluggables) moves from hyperscaler-exclusive to independent vendor availability; enables mid-market and neocloud operators to build 102.4T fabrics without custom ASICs, reducing capex and time-to-market for AI clusters.
detail: Davisson can move 102.4 terabits of data per second, which Broadcom says was double any other CPO switch available when it launched in October 2025. CPO integration reduces optical interconnect power consumption approximately 70% relative to traditional pluggables, resulting in significant TCO and sustainability wins for hyperscale and AI data centers. Micas' announcement is operationally significant because it breaks the pattern where only Meta, NVIDIA, and other hyperscalers could deploy CPO: now mid-sized data center operators and AI neoclouds can order Tomahawk 6-based systems from an independent ODM and get co-packaged optics without engineering their own switch silicon. Production timing (early 2027) aligns with the next wave of neocloud expansion and supports operators who want to reduce per-port optical power without building custom hardware.

title: Yandex outage: Data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
headline: Malicious bots moved to other hosts during Yandex outage
summary: Following Ukrainian drone strikes on three Yandex data centers between October 7-11, Cloudflare analyzed traffic telemetry and found that while search crawler traffic collapsed 99% and cloud services 90%, malicious bot automation did not disappear—it migrated to alternative Russian hosting providers with identical bot fingerprints and continued operating.
why: Demonstrates how BGP-observable infrastructure outages route malicious automation elsewhere rather than stopping it; shows the limits of traffic-based inference for operational security posture.
detail: Cloudflare separated traffic from Yandex's two ASNs to clarify what actually happened. AS13238 (Yandex Search) lost 99% of traffic—almost entirely verified search crawlers indexing content. AS200350 (Yandex.Cloud) dropped 90%, but the key finding was that bot requests to gambling customer accounts fell to zero from Yandex infrastructure immediately after October 8, then reappeared with identical request signatures from Selectel and Radist ASNs. This showed the automation moved, not ceased. Using Cloudflare Radar and Bot Management data, the analysis separated legitimate indexing (93.6% of Yandex Search bot traffic came from verified crawlers) from malicious automation that adapted to infrastructure disruption. The incident highlights how AS-level visibility reveals traffic patterns but can mislead when analyzed in aggregate—a critical distinction for network operations teams tracking bot infrastructure and understanding how routing changes propagate across autonomous systems.

title: Defense Without Detours: Introducing Fastly Network Protect
headline: Fastly launches layer 3 and 4 DDoS filtering service
summary: Fastly launched Network Protect, a Layer 3/4 DDoS defense service that filters unwanted traffic at the edge using the company's 622 Tbps global network capacity—nearly 20 times the largest recorded DDoS attack—with rule-based filtering and planned integration of an Adaptive Threat Engine for automated volumetric attack mitigation.
why: Adds edge-based L3/4 DDoS filtering to Fastly's platform with global scale and zero traffic detours; operationally relevant for teams managing multi-CDN strategies and volumetric attack resilience.
detail: Network Protect uses Fastly's full 622 Tbps network capacity to absorb and filter layer 3 and 4 attacks inline, before traffic reaches origin infrastructure. The service launches with rule-based network traffic filtering and is designed to evolve with network-layer variants of the Adaptive Threat Engine, Fastly's automated mitigation system. The scale comparison is concrete: Fastly's capacity (622 Tbps) dwarfs Cloudflare (534 Tbps), AWS (100+ Tbps), and the largest recorded DDoS attack (roughly 30 Tbps). Fastly noted the product is the beginning of a broader vision including enhanced telemetry-driven automated mitigation. For SRE and NetOps teams, this represents an infrastructure choice point: filtering at the CDN edge versus origin-based mitigation, with clear throughput implications for attack scenarios and normal traffic patterns. The product roadmap includes rule-based filtering today with AI-driven decisions coming later.

title: Palo Alto Networks: Active Exploitation of CVE-2026-0322 (PAN-OS RCE) and CVE-2026-0257 (GlobalProtect Auth Bypass)
headline: Attackers exploit PAN-OS flaws to reach vCenter management
summary: Palo Alto disclosed two critical PAN-OS flaws: CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS 8.6 RCE requiring credentials), actively exploited targeting PA/VM-Series and Panorama appliances; CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS 7.8 auth bypass in GlobalProtect) where ransomware groups are bypassing MFA and pivoting directly to vCenter management. Updated threat intelligence shows attackers moving from gateway compromise to virtualization infrastructure.
why: Firewall management interfaces and VPN gateways are active attack vectors in production; both flaws demand immediate patching and restrict management plane access to trusted IPs only.
detail: Unit 42's October 19 update to the CVE-2026-0257 threat brief reveals new attack tactics: Qilin and Settra ransomware groups are successfully bypassing MFA on GlobalProtect VPN endpoints, establishing initial foothold, then directly targeting vCenter. The flaw affects PAN-OS 10.2.0, 11.1.0, 11.2.0, and 12.1.0, plus Prisma Access versions 10.2.0 and 11.2.0. For CVE-2026-0322, attackers with valid credentials and network access to the management interface achieve root code execution on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama appliances. CISA added both to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; federal agencies must remediate CVE-2026-0322 by October 17. Organizations should apply vendor patches immediately, restrict management interface access to internal IP ranges only, and implement network segmentation to isolate firewall management traffic. The escalation from initial VPN access to hypervisor compromise reflects a material change in post-breach adversary behavior beyond simple lateral movement.

title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway: CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8 RCE) Actively Exploited via Malicious Attachments
headline: Cisco email gateway flaw exploited through crafted attachments
summary: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76519, a critical arbitrary file write vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in Secure Email Gateway's Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) when File Reputation service is enabled and Content Scanner Tools is older than 25.3.0.5525. Unauthenticated attackers send crafted email attachments, write arbitrary files, and execute commands as root on physical and virtual appliances.
why: Email gateways are security infrastructure perimeter devices; root compromise exposes credentials, cryptographic material, and provides pivot path to internal networks. Requires immediate Content Scanner Tools update or AsyncOS version upgrade.
detail: Cisco discovered the flaw internally during security scanning; exploitation became active in October 2026. The vulnerability stems from improper handling of email attachments when AMP's File Reputation service processes them. Attack path is simple: malicious attachment bypasses file analysis when scanner tools are outdated, leading to file write and root execution. CISA added CVE-2026-76519 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities on October 14, requiring federal agencies to patch by October 17. Cisco shipped fixes on September 14 in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780; organizations must upgrade all affected gateways immediately. Attackers with root access can remove local logs and evade detection; network-level logging outside the appliance is essential for forensics. For orgs on AsyncOS 16.0, the fixer for this CVE differs from the September SQL injection patch, requiring careful version verification.

title: Juniper Networks October 2026 Security Bulletins: Multiple CVSS 9.8 RCE Flaws in Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved
headline: Juniper patches five critical remote code execution flaws in Junos
summary: Juniper released October 2026 security bulletins covering dozens of critical Junos OS vulnerabilities including five CVSS 9.8 flaws affecting SRX Series and Junos OS Evolved platforms: CVE-2026-102182 (MX Series certificate-based IKE RCE), CVE-2026-101954 (full device takeover via J-Web), CVE-2026-101986 (pre-authentication CGI execution), CVE-2026-102175 (service-deployment RCE/DoS), CVE-2026-33792 (GRE tunnel stack buffer overflow). CVE-2026-102084 (CVSS 8.1) allows authenticated remote code execution in ADVPN daemon via malformed attributes.
why: Firewall and routing infrastructure must be patched immediately; J-Web management interface and IKE/ADVPN services are network-facing and frequently exposed; unauthenticated remote RCE on routing platforms is critical for BGP integrity.
detail: The five CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities span different attack vectors: Certificate-based IKE packets trigger root-level code execution on MX Series with SPC3; unauthenticated network attackers achieve full device takeover when J-Web is enabled; pre-authentication CGI execution via J-Web; service-deployment processing flaws enable RCE or DoS; and GRE tunnel processing allows stack buffer overflow for root execution. CVE-2026-102084 (CVSS 8.1) is particularly notable for ADVPN deployments—requires authenticated access but allows complete device control if an attacker has compromised a peer or acquired the shared secret. None are currently exploited in the wild. Fixed versions vary by CVE and Junos branch (23.2R2-S7.7, 23.4R2-S8.13, 24.2R2-S5.5 are common fix points). Organizations should upgrade SRX Series and MX Series platforms immediately and validate J-Web is disabled unless explicitly required for management. ADVPN users should audit peer authentication and shared secret management.

title: Boomi Acquires Elementary Data for $40M+ to Add Data Observability and Governance for AI Pipelines
headline: Boomi buys Elementary Data for data pipeline observability
summary: Boomi announced acquisition of Elementary Data for approximately $40-45 million in cash and stock, adding data observability, quality, and governance capabilities to the Boomi Enterprise Platform. Elementary, founded in 2022 as an open-source project, is now adopted by 1,500+ data teams with 1.1M+ monthly downloads.
why: As enterprises operationalize AI agents and workflows, data quality and governance become critical bottlenecks; Elementary's observability tools flag data anomalies before they reach models or automated systems, directly improving AI reliability.
detail: Elementary provides unified observability, quality, governance, and discovery tools for data pipelines. Founded in 2022 as an open-source project, it achieved adoption by 1,500+ data teams with 1.1M+ monthly downloads and a ~4,000-member community before launching Elementary Cloud in 2024 with enterprise-grade capabilities. Elementary builds software that monitors data quality and reliability moving through enterprise pipelines, flagging anomalies before they reach dashboards, models or automated systems. The 17-person team, all based in Israel, joins Boomi; this is Boomi's third Israeli acquisition. Following the Lunar.dev acquisition, Elementary strengthens the Boomi Enterprise Platform with observability capabilities enterprises need to deliver trusted data for AI agents. Boomi confirmed no immediate changes to the open-source repository, release process or community use following the acquisition.

title: Prevalent AI appoints JD Sherry as Chief Revenue Officer
headline: Prevalent AI names JD Sherry chief revenue officer
summary: Prevalent AI appointed JD Sherry as Chief Revenue Officer, leading global go-to-market organization across sales, marketing, and partnerships. Sherry joins from ISTARI, where he was Managing Partner and Global Head of Sales advising boards on cyber resilience.
why: CRO appointment supports Prevalent AI's expansion beyond cybersecurity into wider AI context platform market following $22 million growth investment.
detail: Prevalent AI appointed JD Sherry as Chief Revenue Officer, leading the company's global go-to-market organization across sales, marketing, and partnerships. Sherry joins from ISTARI, where he was Managing Partner and Global Head of Sales advising executive leadership teams and boards on cyber resilience. He brings nearly three decades of cybersecurity experience and has served on boards of several ISTARI portfolio companies, including Prevalent AI since 2021. Prior to ISTARI, Sherry was Chief Strategy Officer and CRO at Remediant, Inc., and held leadership roles at Optiv, Cavirin and Trend Micro. The appointment follows Prevalent AI's recent $22 million growth investment from Integrity Growth Partners, which is funding global expansion, deeper leadership team, and extension of its Data Fabric and Knowledge Graph beyond cybersecurity into wider use cases requiring trusted enterprise context.

title: AI Transforms Radio Networks – AT&T and Verizon Innovations
headline: AT&T and Verizon run AI inside radio network optimisation
summary: AT&T uses AI across planning, forecasting, deployment, and network optimization, with trials with Ericsson delivering significant improvements in throughput and spectral efficiency. Verizon combines centralized rApps for slower network intelligence tasks with local AI inside the gNodeB for faster decisions, achieving better downlink spectral efficiency through AI-based link adaptation.
why: Both carriers report field-validated performance gains from AI-RAN tools, signaling move from pilots to production deployment that will shape network automation strategies for operators.
detail: Operators are moving artificial intelligence deeper into the radio access network, with AT&T and Verizon reporting real performance gains from AI-based RAN tools shared at RCR Wireless News's Telco AI Forum 2026. AT&T's RAN technology team outlines current AI use cases across planning, forecasting, deployment, and network optimization, applying rApps across parts of the network lifecycle to support automation and help engineers manage growing network complexity. AT&T trials with Ericsson delivered significant improvements in throughput and spectral efficiency—gains that matter because spectrum remains costly and limited. Verizon is combining two approaches: centralized rApps handle slower network intelligence tasks while local AI inside the gNodeB supports faster decisions near the radio site. Verizon saw better downlink spectral efficiency through AI-based link adaptation, and another field trial also improved coverage, pointing to stronger user experiences without always adding new sites. Verizon wants AI features to beat current rule-based methods—rule-based systems follow fixed instructions, while AI can adjust from patterns. Both operators emphasize the transition from experimental deployments to production use, setting expectations that field-validated AI-RAN is now the reference architecture rather than emerging research.

title: SNS Telecom & IT report on RAN Automation: Opportunities, Challenges, Strategies and Forecasts
headline: Brownfield operators accelerate non-real-time RIC rollouts across cell sites
summary: SMO/Non-RT RIC adoption is accelerating among brownfield operators including AT&T, Verizon, Telus, Vodafone, DT, Swisscom, STC, NTT DoCoMo, Chunghwa Telecom and Telstra to enable network-wide automation across thousands of cell sites. Annual spending on AI-RAN automation and optimization software and services is expected to grow at CAGR of 9% over the next four years, reaching $1.1 billion by end of 2030.
why: Documents concrete RAN automation adoption across major carriers globally, confirming SMO/RIC as enabling architecture and providing market sizing for network ops teams evaluating AI-RAN automation roadmaps.
detail: SMO/Non-RT RIC adoption is accelerating among brownfield operators to enable network-wide automation across thousands of cell sites through vendor-supplied, third-party and internally developed rApps, with RAN vendors and application developers including Nokia, NVIDIA, Radisys, IS-Wireless, Cohere Technologies, DeepSig and others already committed to support the E3 interface. An alternative path vendors are pursuing is proprietary AI-enabled, real-time optimization capabilities as software upgrades to existing RAN platforms through subscription-based licensing models. The report identifies two distinct deployment strategies: centralized orchestration via SMO/RIC platforms and distributed embedded AI. AI-RAN automation market growth is largely driven by growing investments in centrally coordinated SMO/RIC-enabled automation at the network level and AI-for-RAN software upgrades for embedded real-time intelligence replacing static rule-based algorithms. The adoption curve among named carriers demonstrates that RAN automation is transitioning from selective pilots to broad enterprise deployments.

title: The week in AI-native telco (10-16 Oct 2026)
headline: Scaleway commits three billion euros to European AI infrastructure
summary: Telcos and technology partners pressed ahead with efforts to develop sovereign AI infrastructure and autonomous network deployments. Scaleway, the cloud and AI unit of European telco Iliad Group, is investing in new infrastructure deployments in Scandinavia with €3bn committed to AI-dedicated infrastructure and platforms via its datacentre division OpCore and Scaleway.
why: European telcos are moving beyond network automation to build sovereign AI infrastructure, with material capex commitments creating new operational and procurement implications for network ops teams.
detail: Telcos and technology partners pressed ahead with efforts to develop sovereign AI infrastructure, identify opportunities for autonomous network deployments, and bring agentic AI to bear across networks, enterprise services and SME markets, with standards bodies moving to shape the emerging AI infrastructure landscape while cybersecurity and datacentre interconnect capacity featured prominently. Scaleway, the cloud and AI unit of European telco Iliad Group, is investing in new infrastructure deployments in Scandinavia, expanding its compute capacity and positioning itself to be a key provider of digital sovereign cloud and AI services in Europe, backed by telecom and tech entrepreneur Xavier Niel and Iliad's success as an alternative telco. Iliad committed €3bn into AI-dedicated infrastructure and platforms via its datacentre division OpCore, a joint venture with InfraVia, and Scaleway. This signals a shift in European telco strategy: rather than merely automating existing networks, carriers are building AI-native infrastructure as a platform play to serve enterprise customers seeking alternatives to hyperscaler-dependent architectures.

title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: October 17 update with improved reasoning, coding agents, and public search API access
headline: DeepSeek updates Flash model and opens search API
summary: DeepSeek released V4.1 Flash-1017 on October 17, updating its Flash model with improvements in reasoning, coding, agent tasks and visual understanding. DeepSeek's proprietary search API is now formally available to developers via API starting October 17.
why: The model offers stronger benchmark performance, faster task completion, and shorter outputs, with open MIT-licensed weights available for self-hosted deployment.
detail: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is an updated version of the existing V4.1-Flash model released October 17, 2026, not a separate model family. The October 17 release improved performance across multiple benchmarks (HLE 42.6, DeepSWE 77.0, ProgramBench 29.1, Automation-Bench 60.5) while reducing task runtime and output length. The experiential improvement in agentic coding scenarios is striking, with the model trained using self-feedback reinforcement learning to enhance its ability to build complete projects from scratch, supporting "wish-based" programming tasks. The update is live across DeepSeek's web, app, and API endpoints simultaneously. Model weights are available on Hugging Face under the MIT license, with inference code and deployment instructions enabling developers to run the model on their own infrastructure.

title: US rebrands AI safety apparatus as 'super intelligence' promotion; EU activates enforcement powers amid regulatory divergence
headline: US and EU AI rules diverge for multinational developers
summary: The US rebranded its AI safety apparatus with an explicit mandate to resist foreign regulation of American AI, while the EU activated enforcement powers. This divergence creates a compliance asymmetry that multinational AI developers must navigate: what satisfies US policy expectations may actively conflict with EU legal obligations.
why: The convergence of accelerating AI adoption, active enforcement, and public skepticism creates a governance pressure cooker. Organizations positioning AI governance as a competitive differentiator are best positioned to navigate this environment.
detail: The US rebranded its AI safety apparatus as 'super intelligence' promotion with an explicit mandate to resist foreign regulation of American AI, while the EU activated enforcement powers and MEPs called for binding AI liability legislation. Executive Order 14434 directed NIST to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence,' renaming CAISI to CAISSI with a mandate that includes guarding against 'burdensome and unnecessary regulation of American technologies by foreign governments.' A new EU report published October 14, 2026 found that AI use has increased to 18% in firms in EU strategic sectors, more than doubling in almost every sector. This represents a fundamental shift in how regulatory frameworks are developing: the US is explicitly prioritizing competitive velocity and resisting external constraints, while the EU enforces a comprehensive statutory regime. For multinational enterprises, this means maintaining separate governance tracks—compliance strategies that work in one jurisdiction may create legal exposure in another.

title: Modal Labs lands $750M Series D at $15.75B as AI infrastructure funding hits $2.42B in single week
headline: Modal Labs raises 750 million dollars at 15.75 billion valuation
summary: AI startups announced about $2.42 billion in primary funding across 19 rounds of $20 million or more between October 12 and October 18, 2026. Modal Labs' $750 million Series D was the largest round, at about 31% of the total. AI infrastructure and chips raised about $1.58 billion across five rounds, or 65% of the total.
why: Capital concentration in compute and inference infrastructure reveals where enterprises expect bottlenecks and differentiation in production AI systems. Nearly two-thirds of funding went to infrastructure rather than applications.
detail: AI startups announced about $2.42 billion in primary funding across 19 rounds of $20 million or more between October 12 and October 18, 2026. Modal Labs' $750 million Series D was the largest round, at about 31% of the total. AI infrastructure and chips raised about $1.58 billion across five rounds, or 65% of the total. Modal, Infinigence AI, BlueCore Compute, Salience Labs and Mueon made up the group. The capital allocation is telling: nearly two-thirds of a $2.42B funding week went to infrastructure—compute, serverless platforms, and semiconductors—rather than applications. This reflects mounting conviction that the real margin will accrue to providers controlling inference capacity and model routing, particularly as enterprises move from pilot to production deployment. The concentration also signals investor confidence that these infrastructure plays can sustain premium valuations as model costs compress and latency becomes the differentiator.

title: Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA: Rack-Scale AI for Neo Clouds and Sovereign AI Solution Overview
headline: Cisco and NVIDIA ship rack-scale AI fabric to 73,728 GPUs
summary: Cisco and NVIDIA released NCP-RA (NVIDIA Collective Communications Platform – Reference Architecture) compliant rack-scale AI factory platform, orderable October 2026, scaling to 73,728 GPUs with Cisco Silicon One N9300 front-end and Spectrum-X N9100 back-end fabrics unified under Nexus One architecture.
why: First vendor-neutral NCP-RA reference architecture from non-NVIDIA partner using proprietary silicon; enables neo-cloud and sovereign cloud operators to deploy standardized, multi-tenant rack-scale AI without NVIDIA-exclusive networking hardware.
detail:
Cisco published October 13 technical collateral confirming that its Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA rack-scale platform is orderable from authorized channel partners starting October 2026. This marks the first NCP-RA compliance achievement by an NVIDIA technology partner using its own networking silicon. The architecture combines Cisco Silicon One G300-powered N9300 systems for front-end (scale-up) fabric with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet–silicon based N9100 series for back-end (scale-out) networking, unified under the Nexus One architecture.

The reference architecture scales to 73,728 GPUs—equivalent to 1,024 Vera Rubin NVL72 racks—deployed as a multi-tenant AI factory. Operational management flows through Cisco Cloud Control, providing unified provisioning, monitoring, and lifecycle management. For sovereign and neo-cloud deployments, this architecture enables independent cloud operators to procure standardized NCP-compliant components without lock-in to NVIDIA-exclusive networking stacks. The platform supports both NX-OS (Cisco's flagship OS) and SONiC (open networking OS), allowing operators to preserve existing automation and skills.

For infrastructure operators: this announces production availability and streamlines procurement. Cisco's position as the first non-NVIDIA vendor with NCP-RA compliance on own silicon signals broader ecosystem competition. Channel partners (Supermicro and others) can now quote Cisco-based AI factories as an alternative to NVIDIA's tightly integrated Spectrum-X platforms, particularly for regions or operators requiring multi-vendor optionality.

title: Is RPKI becoming harmful to BGP stability?
headline: Eleven years of data question whether RPKI destabilizes BGP
summary: LACNIC/APNIC analysis examines over 11 years of RPKI and BGP data to measure correlation between routing activity and RPKI-related changes, questioning whether growing RPKI deployment could destabilize routing.
why: Rapid RPKI adoption may create cascading validation failures or misconfigured ROAs; operators must understand if deployment patterns threaten BGP stability at 70%+ coverage.
detail: This analysis addresses a counterintuitive risk: as RPKI adoption accelerates globally, misconfigured ROAs or cascading RPKI validation failures could destabilize inter-domain routing. The research uses RIPE Archive data and RPKI-Flutter—which collects RPKI events from geographically distributed validators at high frequency—to quantify correlation between RPKI state changes and BGP instability. This matters because it challenges assumptions that RPKI is purely additive; operators need to understand whether certain deployment patterns or mass ROA updates create routing churn. With RPKI-valid routing jumping from 54% to 70.3% in one year, driven largely by China's adoption, any systemic RPKI misconfiguration now impacts vastly larger share of global Internet traffic. The practical implication for operators is that RPKI validation enforcement requires careful monitoring of ROA lifecycle and coordination across multiple validators to avoid synchronized failures.

title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
headline: Cloudflare cuts HTTP telemetry pipeline from 9GB/s to under 2GB/s
summary: Cloudflare engineering post details data pipeline optimization: sampling applied upstream, replication rearchitected, aggregations introduced—reducing HTTP dataset from 9+ GB/s to <2 GB/s compressed, achieving ~80% wire reduction.
why: Sampling moved upstream and aggregation deferred to pipeline ingestion; resilient failure handling routes traffic to surviving regions without backpressure when inter-DC links fail.
detail: This post details practical strategies for managing exponential data growth in large-scale observability platforms. Cloudflare iterated through multiple phases: broke monolithic schema (2022), adjusted compression (2024), rearchitected replication (spring 2026), decentralized sampling (summer 2026), and introduced aggregations (fall 2026). The key insight is that sampling now happens at ingestion rather than tail-end: Logfwdrs send single copy to centralized receivers, which apply sampling before buffering, carrying only compacted stream. This reduces wide-area transit load orders of magnitude. Aggregation trades granularity for cost by measuring unique IP counts per minute and summing HTTP methods per domain per verb, avoiding pipeline tail-end computation. For SRE teams managing observability at scale, this demonstrates how to handle petabyte-scale analytics by shifting compute leftward; resilience improves because isolated DC clusters continue ingesting without backpressure when backbone links blip, and non-affected regions route around isolated failures automatically.

title: Weekly Security Roundup: October 7 to 14, 2026 — Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain and perimeter appliance exploitation
headline: Attackers chain three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws for root
summary: UTA0576 actor chained three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws (led by CVE-2026-104935, CVSS 8.6) to achieve root on VPN appliances, exfiltrate credentials and AD metadata, and run Kerberoasting attacks. CISA added multiple firewall and VPN flaws to the KEV list.
why: VPN appliance compromise enables lateral movement into directory infrastructure; chained authentication-bypass flaws demonstrate attackers pivoting from edge perimeter to core identity systems via credential harvesting and Kerberoasting.
detail: CVE-2026-104935 is an authentication bypass in Ivanti Connect Secure (CVSS 8.6) allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to run arbitrary commands on the VPN appliance. Once inside, UTA0576 extracted credentials stored on the appliance, exfiltrated Active Directory metadata, ran Kerberoasting, captured LDAP traffic, and used Python LDAP tools to hunt for administrator passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, altering logs to hide the intrusion. Two additional zero-days were chained to escalate privileges. This attack demonstrates how VPN appliances serve as beachheads for lateral movement into core infrastructure. CISA also added CVE-2026-0322 (Palo Alto PAN-OS) and CVE-2026-76519 (Cisco Email Gateway) to the KEV list, indicating multiple firewall and mail gateway flaws are under active exploitation simultaneously, compounding remediation pressure across the perimeter.

title: Opsin AI Agent Security Raises $21 Million as Agent Sprawl Tests Traditional Defenses
headline: Opsin raises $21 million to police enterprise AI agent sprawl
summary: Opsin, a San Jose-based AI governance and security startup, raised $21 million led by SYN Ventures and Race Capital to address autonomous software sprawl. The platform monitors AI agents and tools deployed across enterprises, identifying risky components and agent behavior while enforcing policies without blocking legitimate use.
why: Network and SRE teams face new risks from unsanctioned AI agents operating autonomously across infrastructure; Opsin's agent-centric security approach fills a gap traditional security tools cannot address.
detail: Opsin's funding announcement on October 15, 2026 reflects a critical infrastructure gap: enterprises are rapidly deploying AI agents without adequate governance or visibility. Unlike traditional security that monitors network perimeter or endpoint behavior, Opsin targets the new problem: autonomous software accessing systems, data, and integrations broadly. The platform tracks which AI agents are deployed, what skills and components (including model context protocol servers) they rely on, and their actual runtime behavior. For network and infrastructure practitioners, this matters because agents often operate with broad system access and make lateral moves that bypass conventional network segmentation. Opsin claims it can identify potentially dangerous agent activity and enforce policies without disrupting legitimate agent operations. The startup spun up quickly—announced to be addressing a nascent but urgent category in enterprise security. SYN Ventures and Race Capital's backing signals investor conviction that agent governance is as important as the AI infrastructure itself.

title: Rocío Lorenzo named CEO of Telenet, succeeding John Porter; Luk Bruynseels moves to Liberty Global
headline: Roc\u00edo Lorenzo takes over as Telenet chief executive
summary: Rocío Lorenzo becomes CEO of Telenet effective November 2, 2026, succeeding John Porter after 13 years. Separately, Telenet CTO Luk Bruynseels is leaving for a new role at parent company Liberty Global.
why: Leadership transition at major European telecom operator during infrastructure consolidation within Liberty Global's new Benelux group; CTO departure to parent signals organizational restructuring.
detail: Rocío Lorenzo will become CEO of Telenet on November 2, succeeding John Porter after 13 years at the helm of the Belgian telecoms and media operator. Lorenzo joins from Cable & Wireless Panamá, where she served as Executive President and General Manager since January 2024. She will report to Stephen van Rooyen, CEO of Ziggo Group, as Telenet and VodafoneZiggo are brought together within Liberty Global's new Benelux telecommunications group. Porter, 68, will work with Lorenzo for the remainder of 2026 to support the transition. Van Rooyen noted Lorenzo brings more than 20 years of international experience alongside knowledge of the Belgian market. Separately, Telenet group confirmed that chief technology officer Luk Bruynseels is leaving the Belgian operator to take up a new role at parent company Liberty Global.

title: Microsoft Agent Framework Reaches 1.22: Consolidation Around Harness Patterns as AutoGen Enters Maintenance
headline: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.22 retires AutoGen for Harness agents
summary: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) at Python 1.22 and .NET 1.25 replaces AutoGen with production-ready Harness agent, functional workflow API, and channel packages for distributed deployment. AutoGen moved to maintenance mode October 2025 with no new features.
why: Framework consolidation signals industry alignment on harness architecture for operations agents. For teams building bespoke infrastructure agents, MAF is now the canonical replacement with 22 Python minor releases in six months post-1.0.
detail: Microsoft Agent Framework is the open-source Python and .NET SDK, with Go in public preview, that replaces AutoGen and the Semantic Kernel agent APIs. The same teams build it. Six months after 1.0 it has shipped 22 Python minor releases and the core .NET packages are at 1.25. The biggest additions are a batteries-included Harness agent, an experimental Python functional workflow API, channel packages for hosting, and resilient background execution. The Harness agent provides a production-grade base with memory, tools, and context management out of the box. The functional workflow API (experimental in Python) introduces stateful, resumable agent chains—essential for long-running operations workflows that must survive network partitions and restarts. Channel packages enable deployment across stdio, HTTP/SSE, WebSocket, and other transports, critical for distributed agent architectures in infrastructure environments. AutoGen was originally developed by Microsoft but placed into maintenance mode in October 2025 with no new features being added.

title: AI in the RAN moves toward the scale test
headline: AT&T and Verizon push AI into live RAN processing
summary: AT&T and Verizon executives described AI-based RAN deployments producing measurable results while emphasizing economic and operational constraints for scale deployment. AT&T uses AI at scale across planning, forecasting, deployment, configuration, and network optimization; Verizon is moving AI into real-time gNodeB processing.
why: Shifts focus from proving AI-RAN works to determining ROI at production scale; defines 'AI worthiness' test where performance gains must outweigh computing cost and complexity.
detail: For AT&T and Verizon, the next stage is less about proving technology works than determining where it creates enough value to justify deployment at scale. AT&T has trialed Ericsson's AI-native link adaptation feature and seen significant improvements in throughput and spectral efficiency. Verizon sees particular potential in moving AI beyond centralized functions into real-time processing at the gNodeB, creating an 'AI worthiness' test where any performance or user-experience improvement must outweigh additional computing cost and complexity introduced into the network. Moving beyond trials requires open architectures, automation, and disciplined lifecycle management across distributed networks. Both operators stress that AI must deliver meaningful ROI to justify scale deployment. This marks an inflection point: the technical proof-of-concept phase is ending and procurement decisions will hinge on disciplined TCO analysis rather than engineering feasibility.

title: Versioned metrics: Shipping the first Release Candidate metrics in hostmetrics
headline: OpenTelemetry ships first release candidate process metrics in hostmetrics
summary: OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib v0.160.0 released October 13, 2026, shipping first Release Candidate process semantic conventions metrics in hostmetrics receiver's process scraper, moving toward stable v1 process metrics.
why: Ops/SRE teams can now standardize on stable process-level observability; RC metrics enable community validation before stable release, accelerating adoption of standardized process telemetry.
detail: OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib v0.160.0 (released October 13, 2026) advances the project's maturity for host-level observability. The System SIG has worked for over a year to stabilize process metrics semantics—the dataset describing CPU, memory, disk, and I/O at the process level. The RC designation signals that the specification is feature-complete and expected to be stable, though community feedback is actively solicited during the RC period. For SREs and AIOps practitioners, this is significant because it means you can now standardize on a single, vendor-neutral semantic for process metrics across your observability stack. The hostmetrics receiver's process scraper now emits metrics using the RC semantic conventions, replacing previous iterations. This aligns with OpenTelemetry's May 2026 CNCF graduation and the stabilization of all three core signals (metrics, logs, traces). Operators deploying OTel can confidently use process metrics in production, knowing that semantic definitions will not break in the transition from RC to v1, reducing future migration overhead.

title: NetBox Labs Partners with NVIDIA and Grafana: Infrastructure Intelligence for AI Datacenters
headline: NetBox Labs links source of truth to NVIDIA and Grafana
summary: NetBox Labs announced partnerships with NVIDIA Config Manager and Grafana Labs, expanding the NetBox Infrastructure Intelligence Platform to support AI datacenter operations with enhanced observability and configuration management integrations.
why: Directly addresses network source-of-truth integration with AI infrastructure automation—critical for operators managing large-scale AI datacenter deployments.
detail: NetBox Labs published three major announcements: (1) NVIDIA partnership for AI datacenter deployment and operations, integrating NVIDIA Config Manager; (2) Grafana Labs partnership for enhanced network and datacenter infrastructure observability; and (3) NetBox Designs public preview to reduce manual entry in network builds. These moves position NetBox as the system of record for AI hyperscale operations. For NetDevOps practitioners, this means tighter integration between your network source of truth (NetBox as IPAM/DCIM), AI infrastructure automation (NVIDIA), and observability (Grafana)—eliminating hand-offs between teams. The Designs feature directly reduces toil in day-1 network provisioning by automating the design-to-deploy workflow. Platform MCP (Model Context Protocol) is now generally available, enabling AI agents to act on intent through a structured interface.

title: The Future Is Now: How AI-Driven Automation Is Transforming Network Operations
headline: Itential maps shift from static runbooks to agent-driven network ops
summary: Itential published a practitioner-focused guide on deploying AI across network and infrastructure, covering the shift from static runbooks to agent-driven operations with human-in-the-loop controls and intent-first network design.
why: Shows the practical operationalization of AI agents in network automation—from experimental assistants to autonomous, governed operations—directly applicable to AIOps and NetDevOps practice.
detail: Joksan Flores (Itential Principal Solutions Engineer, formerly Cisco networking architect) outlines the 2026 reality of AI in network operations. Three key themes: (1) Agent-Driven Operations—agents replace static runbooks by negotiating, validating, and escalating intelligently; engineers supervise, refine intent models, and approve high-impact changes. (2) Intent-First Networking—engineers define outcomes (performance, security, resilience), and agent-driven systems determine execution across vendors, domains, and layers. (3) The missing pieces are now available: MCP (Model Context Protocol), modern AI agents, A2A protocols, and orchestration platforms. For teams building NetDevOps workflows, this is the roadmap: start with high-fidelity intent models (Nautobot Jobs, Itential FlowAgent Builder), wire in human gates (especially for production), and let agents handle the cross-domain orchestration. The post specifically addresses the 2026 gap: AI agents work well in labs, but production requires fail-safe design—rollback capabilities, human checkpoints, and structured intent validation. Updated October 15, 2026.

title: OCP 2026: AI Infrastructure Moves From Scaling to Coordination
headline: Oracle urges standard interfaces between AI data centres and grids
summary: At OCP Summit 2026, Oracle called for standardized interfaces between AI data centers and power grids; Microsoft, Oracle, HPE, Intel, and Google described an emerging need to coordinate computing, networking, power, cooling, and operations as unified architecture.
why: Network infrastructure planning must now account for energy efficiency, grid integration, and system-level optimization—not just throughput and latency.
detail: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VP Pradeep Vincent called for industry-wide standards governing how large-scale AI data centers interact with electrical grids, emphasizing energy efficiency, cooling reliability, and responsible infrastructure development. Microsoft outlined its Maia 300 roadmap and full-stack co-design strategy to optimize AI inference performance per watt and per dollar. Intel and HPE emphasized heterogeneous, workload-specific computing architectures rather than one-size-fits-all design. OCI Supercluster now scales beyond 100,000 NVIDIA GB200 Superchips or 800,000 to 1 million GPUs for large-scale training and inference, combining bare-metal GPUs with high-speed RDMA networking. This reflects maturation of the field: after years of raw capacity expansion, operators now prioritize system-level efficiency metrics and grid-aware resource management.

title: OcNOS Goes 102.4T: IP Infusion Announces Support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Platforms
headline: IP Infusion OcNOS adds Broadcom Tomahawk 6 at 102.4 terabits
summary: IP Infusion announced OcNOS-DC support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6, enabling 102.4 Tbps fabric with 512 ports of 200G, supporting scale-up clusters of 128,000 XPUs in a two-layer leaf-spine topology.
why: Eliminates super-spine layers and reduces hop count, cutting latency and optics cost while maintaining lossless RoCEv2 at full line rate for AI workloads.
detail: OcNOS-DC on Tomahawk 6 delivers native 1.6T ports supporting scale-up networks connecting 512 accelerators in a single hop, while scale-out clusters reach 128,000 XPUs in a two-layer leaf-spine design. A flatter fabric topology reduces hops at every scale: for scale-up, twice the capacity in every switch means fewer devices in the traffic path; for scale-out, eliminating the super-spine layer dramatically lowers latency. OcNOS-DC provides Priority Flow Control (PFC) and Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) to maintain lossless RoCEv2 transport at full line rate. With 512×200G ports, operators can connect more accelerators per leaf and build larger clusters with fewer switches. Scale-across topologies benefit from 1.6T and 800G uplinks feeding interconnect platforms running OcNOS, keeping data-center-to-data-center capacity in sync with growing intra-cluster demands.

title: Pluto Security Emerges from Stealth with $42M Series A to Govern Enterprise AI Tool Use
headline: Pluto Security leaves stealth with $42M to govern AI tools
summary: Pluto Security emerged from stealth with $42M in total funding ($8.5M seed led by TLV Partners, $34M Series A led by Jump Capital) to secure AI applications and agentic workflows at the endpoint level. The platform monitors AI tool interactions, detects exposed credentials in milliseconds using custom small language models, and can intervene in real time across browsers, desktop apps, and agent workflows.
why: Infrastructure and security ops teams managing AI agent deployment now have a baseline endpoint security control for agentic workflows expanding across enterprises.
detail: Pluto Security combines endpoint visibility, contextual AI interaction analysis, and real-time policy enforcement to monitor how employees and AI agents use AI tools. The platform runs proprietary small language models on endpoints to classify tasks and detect sensitive data exposure—distinguishing between legitimate schema references and credential leaks—returning decisions in milliseconds. Unlike traditional DLP systems, Pluto can inject context back into sessions to prompt agent confirmation before risky permissions escalations. The founding team includes engineers from Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, and browser security backgrounds. The company reports $2M+ ARR and serves Fortune 500 organizations including Oscar Health, Workato, Sixt, and AlphaSense. Early adoption data shows 60% of detected AI security risks originate from non-developer-authored applications, with finance, marketing, and legal departments as the largest risk sources. The platform integrates with Cisco Agent Builder via MCP and Anthropic's Claude Compliance API, positioning it as an infrastructure control point for the emerging agentic enterprise stack.

title: Harmonic Security Raises $50M Series B to Govern Workforce AI Interactions and Data Exposure
headline: Harmonic Security raises $50M to watch workforce AI data exposure
summary: Harmonic Security raised $50M Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, bringing total funding to $76M. Its platform runs custom small language models to inspect employee interactions with AI tools in browsers, desktop apps and agentic workflows, flagging exposed credentials in milliseconds. The company protects more than 100 enterprises with millions of employees globally.
why: Security and ops teams can now govern AI interactions in real time with sub-200ms latency and contextual risk classification, enabling safe AI adoption as autonomous agents proliferate in production.
detail: Harmonic said it will use the new capital to expand its engineering and go-to-market teams in the United States and United Kingdom, growing to more than 90 people across both countries. The platform governs employee use of AI tools in real time by inspecting interactions as they happen and enforcing controls based on what it finds. Harmonic relies on custom small language models rather than giant general-purpose ones, classifying the task an employee is attempting and detecting sensitive data in the exchange. Harmonic puts its latency at about 200ms and claims 96% fewer false positives than traditional data loss prevention systems. The Usage Intelligence layer shows leaders which AI use cases create value, which employees have found faster ways to work, and where to invest next. The company integrates with Cisco Agent Builder via MCP and Anthropic's Claude Compliance API, addressing the gap between blocking risky behavior and enabling productivity in the agentic era.

title: Verizon and Ericsson complete world's first outdoor 6G field call in 7GHz spectrum
headline: Verizon and Ericsson make first outdoor 6G call at 7GHz
summary: Verizon completed first pre-standard 6G field call in 7GHz spectrum band using Ericsson 6G proof-of-concept technology at commercial network site in Concord, California, following earlier ISAC trials.
why: Transition from lab to live-site 6G validation signals near-term spectrum readiness; operators should begin planning RAN modernization and agentic AI integration timelines for next-generation deployment.
detail: Verizon's 6G field trial represents a concrete step beyond isolated lab proofs toward commercial-grade pre-standard validation. The deployment leveraged Ericsson 6G proof-of-concept technology at a live Verizon commercial network site in Concord, California, to establish an outdoor 6G field call in the 7GHz spectrum band. This follows earlier ISAC (integrated sensing and communication) trials conducted with Samsung and Qualcomm. For network engineering teams, the relevance is twofold: first, the move toward outdoor site validation signals that vendors and operators are transitioning from controlled indoor trials to real-world propagation and interference scenarios; second, Verizon's broader 60,000-site vRAN is now applying agentic AI to planned configuration changes, service assurance, and network optimization while calling for industry-wide interoperability standards, suggesting that RAN automation and 6G readiness are being pursued in parallel.

title: Spectrum completes Cox integration and rolls out NVIDIA-powered edge compute across 1,000+ sites
headline: Spectrum deploys NVIDIA edge compute across more than 1,000 sites
summary: Charter's Spectrum brand is rolling out NVIDIA-powered edge compute across 1,000+ sites following Cox acquisition. Spectrum now serves 70+ million locations with edge hubs delivering <10ms latency to 500 million devices.
why: 1,000+ edge compute sites at scale require operators to reassess edge QoS SLAs, backhaul capacity planning, and cloud-to-edge orchestration architecture for distributed GPU inference.
detail: Charter's Spectrum brand is deploying NVIDIA-powered edge compute at over 1,000 sites across its merged footprint, enabling support for robotics, low-latency AI inference, and other latency-sensitive workloads at the edge. Spectrum positions hundreds of megawatts of power from more than 1,000 edge data centers and hubs that are less than 10 milliseconds removed from over 500 million devices in homes and businesses. The scale is notable: Charter's acquisition of Cox's cable assets brought over 11 million former Cox homes and businesses online, expanding Spectrum's total footprint beyond 70 million locations. Charter's virtualization of CMTS paves the way for this work, indicating that centralized packet processing and edge disaggregation are prerequisites for distributed edge GPU deployment. For operators, this deployment model suggests a shift toward treating edge hubs as distributed compute-on-demand platforms, requiring updates to fiber interconnect SLAs, backhaul capacity planning, and edge-to-cloud orchestration policies.

title: RFC 10055: Configuring UDP Sockets for Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) for Common Platforms
headline: New RFC explains how to configure ECN on UDP sockets
summary: RFC 10055 provides guidance on configuring UDP sockets for Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) across common platforms, published as an informational RFC in October 2026. The document addresses practical implementation considerations for ECN deployment in UDP-based applications.
why: Practitioners deploying ECN for congestion management in real-time and delay-sensitive UDP applications need portable, cross-platform socket configuration patterns; this RFC codifies best practices across Linux, Windows, and BSD systems.
detail: RFC 10055, authored by M. Duke, standardizes ECN socket configuration patterns across operating systems. ECN is increasingly critical for modern networking infrastructure, particularly in data center and WAN scenarios where congestion signals enable traffic management without packet loss. However, implementation varies significantly across platforms and network stacks. This RFC reduces deployment friction and improves interoperability. For network operators deploying congestion-aware applications and AIOps systems relying on fast feedback signals, consistent ECN implementation improves observability of network state and enables better demand-responsive traffic engineering.

title: Anthropic Q3 2026 Revenue Hits $16.8B, JPMorgan Chase Restricts AI Agent Access to Customer Accounts
headline: JPMorgan bars outside AI agents from customer accounts
summary: Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, up 45% year-over-year. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon announced the bank will not allow outside AI agents to access customer accounts and operate on their behalf.
why: Enterprise adoption is bifurcating—accelerating capex on AI infrastructure clashes with risk-averse policies on autonomous agent access to critical financial systems.
detail: During the week of October 12–18, 2026, two trends emerged: companies selling into AI infrastructure reported strong growth, with Anthropic's Q3 revenue rising 45% to $16.8 billion, while TSMC posted Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion with a 66.4% gross margin. This reflects sustained enterprise demand for AI model capacity and semiconductor infrastructure. However, several major institutions drew boundaries around AI agent autonomy—JPMorgan Chase announced it will not permit outside AI agents to access customer accounts and operate independently on their behalf. This reveals a governance divergence: while AI spending accelerates at the infrastructure layer, financial services and critical operations are implementing explicit restrictions on agentic AI access, signaling regulatory caution and fiduciary risk concerns even as model providers report record revenue growth.

title: Meet Artist: Selector Foundry's Dashboard Agent Builds Live Network Views from Natural Language
headline: Selector launches agent that builds network dashboards from plain language
summary: Selector launched Artist, an agentic NetOps component within Selector Foundry that generates live network dashboards from plain-language requests in seconds, eliminating manual dashboard backlog and query syntax requirements. The agent integrates with Selector's full-stack observability and AIOps foundation to support real-time incident response and NOC workflows.
why: Addresses NOC dashboard request bottlenecks by enabling non-technical operators to generate event-correlation and incident-context views instantly, reducing response time in multi-domain network events.
detail: Selector Foundry represents a shift from traditional AIOps dashboards to agentic NetOps, where specialized AI agents (Rosetta, Loom, TicketMaster, Herald, Artist, Sculptor) collaborate on incident investigation and remediation within one correlated data model. Artist specifically solves a workflow friction point: in war rooms and post-incident reviews, teams repeatedly request custom dashboard views (one incident, one application path, one device context, executive summaries) that arrive too late or require SQL expertise. Artist accepts requests like "show me edge-rtr-3 dependencies during this incident" and builds an interactive dashboard matching the request, refinable in conversation. The platform consolidates raw telemetry (metrics, logs, events, flows, streaming telemetry) through a harmonized data model supporting cross-domain correlation; Selector claims 1,412 signals across three alert clusters resolve to a single incident with root cause (device reboot) visible in the view. This moves network operations from "detect and search" to "detect and context-render automatically," critical for NOCs handling multivendor, multi-domain environments where alert storms obscure root causes across L1–L7.

title: IP Infusion announces OcNOS support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6 platforms at 102.4 Tbps
headline: IP Infusion's OcNOS adds support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6
summary: IP Infusion announced OcNOS-DC network operating system support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6-based platforms, extending support across 40+ open hardware platforms and doubling bandwidth to 102.4 Tbps for next-generation AI and cloud networks with production-grade RoCEv2, dynamic load balancing, and UEC compliance.
why: OcNOS-DC on Tomahawk 6 provides production-grade lossless RoCEv2 and UEC support across multiple ODM platforms, reducing operational friction and training burden for hyperscalers deploying next-gen AI fabric at scale.
detail: OcNOS-DC is a network operating system purpose-built for AI and HPC fabric operations with runtime support for RoCEv2, Priority Flow Control, ECN-based congestion control with DCQCN, dynamic load balancing (DLB) for avoiding hash-based flow collisions, and UEC compliance. Extension to Tomahawk 6 represents significant milestone: Tomahawk 6 delivers 2x throughput jump from Tomahawk 5 (51.2 to 102.4 Tbps), supports native 1.6T ports (up to 64 native 1.6T or 512 × 200G radix for scale-out), and includes options for 200G and 100G PAM4 SerDes depending on copper reach and port density. OcNOS-DC already ships on Tomahawk 4 and Tomahawk 5 in production. Tomahawk 6 support extends OcNOS to 40+ open hardware platforms, giving operators choice in switch ODMs (Micas, Arista, Edge-core, Delta, Wistron) while maintaining single network OS and fabric-control paradigm. Particularly valuable for neocloud providers building GPU data centers at scale who need standardized OS to reduce training and automation burden across heterogeneous hardware deployments.

title: RPKI Now Protects 70% of Internet Routes, Up From 54% a Year Ago
headline: RPKI now protects 70% of internet routes
summary: RPKI-valid routing jumped from 54% to 70.3% in a year, driven largely by China's adoption. Nearly half of all invalid routes reach only a single vantage point, and when wrong networks announce addresses, 71% reach just one peer.
why: Rapid RPKI deployment now protects majority of routes; operators should prioritize ROV implementation and ASPA path validation to keep pace.
detail: RPKI-valid routing jumped from 54% to 70.3% in a year, driven largely by China's adoption. This marks significant acceleration in cryptographic routing security deployment. Of all routed IPv4 space not in RPKI-valid routes, nearly 60% is in the United States, and about one in four addresses belongs to the US Department of Defense. Nearly half of all invalid routes reach only a single vantage point; when wrong networks announce addresses, 71% reach only one. This isolation of invalid routes demonstrates ROV's practical effectiveness at blocking hijacks early. However, IPinfo found thousands of records flagged as failed that were present in every independently validated set they checked, with their routes still RPKI-valid, meaning a count of failing records is not a measure of lost protection. Path validation via ASPA is emerging as the next frontier, with deployment accelerating but still requiring broader router and validator support.

title: Timor-Leste's Internet ecosystem enters a new phase of development with TL-IXP and RPKI initiatives
headline: Timor-Leste builds national IXP with RPKI validation
summary: Timor-Leste is establishing a national IXP (TL-IXP) with integrated RPKI validation, route servers, and DNS root mirrors. Approximately 60% of announced address space is covered by valid ROAs with 34% invalid-route filtering measured.
why: Regional IXP deployment with integrated RPKI validation demonstrates how emerging regions build routing security into new infrastructure; operator readiness metrics show 34% ROV adoption can improve significantly.
detail: The Timor-Leste Internet Exchange Point (TL-IXP) will allow ISPs and other networks to exchange traffic locally rather than routing through international connections. Plans include route servers, DNS root mirrors, monitoring infrastructure, and routing security measures such as RPKI validation. Timor-Leste has made progress in strengthening routing security through RPKI, with approximately 60% of announced address space covered by valid ROAs. ROAs allow network operators to declare which Autonomous Systems are authorized to originate specific IP address prefixes, and Route Origin Validation uses this information to identify and reject invalid route announcements. Over the seven days ending July 10, 2026, APNIC Labs measured invalid-route filtering in Timor-Leste at 34.42%, compared with 14.46% across Southeast Asia and 26.69% globally. While measurements indicate encouraging progress, continued ROA creation and broader implementation of ROV among network operators will be important as Timor-Leste's Internet ecosystem grows and becomes more interconnected.

title: CISA adds Palo Alto CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS 8.6 root RCE) to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
headline: CISA flags exploited root code execution flaw in PAN-OS
summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed CVE-2026-0322, a CVSS 8.6 vulnerability in PAN-OS management interface allowing authenticated attackers with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. CISA added it to KEV catalog with three-day federal remediation deadline.
why: Management interface access with valid credentials now grants full root control of PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls; critical for network ops managing perimeter security and incident response.
detail: CVE-2026-0322 affects PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama (virtual and M-Series); Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access unaffected. Very limited exploitation observed with three IPs identified in advisory. Fixed releases available for PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, 12.2 with 11.2.16 expected October 15. This continues 2026's pattern of firewall management interfaces as primary attack surface, compounding risk for teams still managing unpatched internet-facing PA deployments already exposed to CVE-2026-0257 (GlobalProtect auth bypass), which ransomware groups Qilin and Settra actively exploit.

title: OpenAI appoints Uday Ruddarraju to lead infrastructure and compute business
headline: OpenAI puts Uday Ruddarraju in charge of compute
summary: Uday Ruddarraju, OpenAI's CTO of compute, replaces Sachin Katti to lead the overall compute organization. Katti departs after roughly one year and will continue as an advisor through November 15.
why: Infrastructure leadership changes directly impact OpenAI's ability to execute $750B compute spending plans through 2030, critical for scaling AI model training and inference.
detail: Ruddarraju, previously serving as OpenAI's CTO of compute since July 2026, has been promoted to lead the overall compute organization, replacing Sachin Katti. Ruddarraju, who ran infrastructure at Elon Musk's xAI until July 2025, takes over from Katti, who had been overseeing infrastructure and led the $30B Georgia data center build, and leaves the role within weeks to stay on as an adviser. OpenAI has appointed Ruddarraju to lead its infrastructure and compute businesses, running its Stargate and other data center efforts, after he joined OpenAI last July as head of compute and infrastructure and was named OpenAI's CTO of Compute this July. Ruddarraju's career spans large-scale infrastructure work, including nearly six years at Robinhood rising to Senior Director of Engineering and Head of Infrastructure, over five years at eBay, and foundational work at Amazon Web Services. The consolidation of compute and infrastructure leadership signals OpenAI's prioritization of infrastructure scale during a critical period of capital expansion and technical execution for frontier AI development.

title: Acronis appoints Prakash Panjwani as CEO, replacing Jan-Jaap Jager
headline: Acronis names Prakash Panjwani chief executive
summary: Acronis has appointed Prakash Panjwani as Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately, succeeding Jan-Jaap Jager. Panjwani previously led WatchGuard Technologies and SafeNet, transforming WatchGuard from a firewall vendor into a broader AI-powered cybersecurity platform.
why: CEO change positions Acronis to strengthen its managed service provider market footprint, where 21,000+ service providers rely on its platform to protect 750,000+ businesses across 150 countries.
detail: Acronis has appointed Prakash Panjwani as its new chief executive officer, effective October 15, 2026, replacing Jan-Jaap Jager, who will remain a shareholder. Based in Schaffhausen, Switzerland, Acronis sells software combining cybersecurity, data protection, IT operations, and hybrid infrastructure management, with distribution heavily channel-focused through managed service providers. Panjwani previously served as CEO of WatchGuard Technologies and SafeNet. During his decade at WatchGuard, he oversaw the company's evolution from a firewall-focused business into a broader cybersecurity platform incorporating AI-powered endpoint detection and response (EDR), extended detection and response (XDR), and managed detection and response (MDR). The leadership change comes as Acronis looks to expand its AI-based cybersecurity and data protection business and strengthen its position in the MSP market where service providers use the platform to support over 750,000 businesses globally.

title: NetClaw: Open-Source Network Engineering Agent Presented at MCP Dev Summit Toronto
headline: NetClaw open-source network engineering agent presented at MCP summit
summary: John Capobianco from Itential presented NetClaw, an open-source network engineering agent, at MCP Dev Summit Toronto on October 6, 2026. NetClaw integrates pyATS, MCP, network APIs, observability, security, and documentation into a single agent organized around skills, tools, evidence, and constraints.
why: NetClaw demonstrates a practitioner-led approach to agentic network operations: grounding agent reasoning in deterministic tools (Cisco pyATS), connecting to management systems via MCP, and enforcing operational constraints—a replicable pattern for teams operationalizing agents on real infrastructure.
detail: John Capobianco from Itential developed NetClaw over 18 months after recognizing early that MCP was essential for networking operations. While Itential was connecting AI requests to workflows, validation, and approvals, he independently explored MCP for networking—matching the core question of how to make agents useful on real infrastructure. By February 2026, that became NetClaw, an open network engineering agent integrating pyATS (Cisco's gold-standard network testing framework), MCP, network APIs, observability platforms, security constraints, and documentation into a single open-source project. The agent is organized around skills, tools, evidence, and constraints—enabling it to reason about network state deterministically while respecting operational guardrails. This is a hands-on example of operationalizing agentic network operations: grounding agent reasoning in deterministic tools, connecting to management systems through standard protocols, and enforcing operational constraints. The project is publicly available for teams starting their own network agent implementations.

title: OpenTelemetry Collector v0.163.0 released with Prometheus native histogram mapping stabilization
headline: OpenTelemetry Collector stabilises Prometheus native histogram mapping
summary: OpenTelemetry Collector v0.163.0 released October 14, 2026 with Prometheus exporter stabilizations including native histogram mapping and resource constant labels configuration. Hostmetrics receiver adds release-candidate semantic conventions metrics for process telemetry moving toward stable v1.0.
why: Standardizes process-level observability metrics across platforms; critical for teams building portable monitoring pipelines that move beyond application-only instrumentation.
detail: The v0.163.0 release continues OpenTelemetry's incremental standardization of telemetry collection. The addition of release-candidate semantic conventions for host metrics in the hostmetrics receiver marks progress for infrastructure observability within OTel's standards process. This brings parity to application, infrastructure, and business metrics under one specification framework. The Prometheus exporter compatibility layer sees three stabilizations: content negotiation, native histogram mapping, and resource constant labels configuration. No OTLP wire protocol changes or trace semantics shifts occurred, keeping this release low-risk for existing deployments. For platform teams managing collector fleets at scale, this represents incremental progress toward complete semantic convention coverage without breaking existing telemetry pipelines.

title: October 2026 AI Model Updates: Every Launch, Access Change, and Price Move
headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon ship as GPT-6.1 is cancelled
summary: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched October 7 with 1M context and adaptive thinking at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, Gemini 4 Argon reached general availability October 13, Meta Muse Wonder launched October 12 as Meta's first frontier model, and GPT-6.1 Astra was cancelled.
why: Model consolidation and pricing shifts in the frontier tier affect API cost modeling and competitive landscape for production deployments; track access gates and deprecation deadlines for migration planning.
detail: Anthropic shipped Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7 at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens up to 100K context, positioning it as a low-cost competitor to GPT-6 Luna's sub-$1 tier economics. Google's Gemini 4 Argon reached general availability on October 13 after launching to vetted cyber defenders, now broadly available across paid API tiers and consumer subscriptions. Meta Superintelligence Labs shipped Muse Wonder on October 12 as Meta's first frontier models positioned head-to-head with OpenAI and Anthropic at $4/$20. Mistral Large 4 was previewed October 6 behind a guardrailed Studio with no published price, licence or architecture, and weights due end of month—marking a shift from September's volume releases to gated frontier entries. xAI released Grok Voice 3.0 on October 14. This reflects consolidation: after September's 20+ releases in two weeks, October pivoted to targeted launches with stricter access controls and pricing tiering that requires production cost recalibration.

title: IBM Study: Eight in Ten EMEA Enterprises Escalate AI Incidents to Board or C-Suite as AI Agents Test Governance
headline: Most EMEA firms escalate AI incidents to the board
summary: AI-related incidents are reaching boardrooms across Europe and the Middle East, with 80% of executives reporting board or C-suite escalation in the past year, yet only 40% changed AI governance policy in response. 75% expect AI agents to have autonomy by 2027, but only 37% say governance is designed to scale with agentic AI deployment.
why: Governance capabilities and risk accountability are not keeping pace with adoption, creating operational and regulatory risk for enterprises deploying AI at scale.
detail: The survey found that 80% of EMEA executives experienced AI-related incidents reaching their board or C-suite in the past year, with only 40% changing AI governance policy or frameworks in response. This disconnect between incident frequency and governance response reflects a critical maturity gap. 75% of respondents expect AI agents to have some level of autonomy with respect to decisions by 2027, yet only 37% say their governance is designed to scale with agentic AI deployment. Only 37% of respondents have a formal, board-reviewed quantification of the financial risks created by gaps in their AI governance. The research highlights that enterprises are deploying autonomous AI faster than their governance frameworks can adapt, creating exposure to regulatory and operational risk. Supply chain visibility is also weak: 54% of respondents acknowledge gaps or limitations in how their governance framework covers AI systems and models used by key vendors and technology partners.

title: Cisco at OCP 2026: Silicon One, NVIDIA Optics and the Network Behind AI
headline: Cisco Silicon One P200 ships in Microsoft and Alibaba networks
summary: Cisco's Silicon One P200 is in hyperscale production at Microsoft and Alibaba. Cisco and NVIDIA's new USFP optics claim 4x bandwidth density and 1.3x power efficiency with planned open multi-source specification.
why: Cisco's open networking strategy has production deployments validating multi-vendor Ethernet momentum; Acacia optics acquisition and SONiC adoption indicate platform credibility for hyperscale AI clusters.
detail: Cisco demonstrated production momentum at OCP 2026 on multiple fronts.
